correctness.rationale: TR-BDF2 stability map is derived from its source. Periodization supplies the exact cyclic Green kernel; the resolvent derivative identity gives G^2 and a strictly positive off-diagonal sign margin, reducing positivity to a diagonal Chebyshev condition. An exact three-interval Bernstein certificate proves n=7 positive for every step, hence all n<=7. An exact n=8 strict negative witness, monotonicity in n, and strict convexity of 1/U_{n-1} give exactly one failure window for n>=8. Hyperbolic scaling proves endpoints and the quadratic limiting return law. Standalone verify.py rerun passed all 24 exact Bernstein certificates, 234 Fourier comparisons, and four endpoint brackets; finite checks are not the universal proof.

value.rationale: Exact all-step positivity on seven or fewer cycle states for an L-stable second-order time integrator, followed by loss and recovery at larger cycle sizes, is a meaningful boundary not captured by general SSP sufficiency. A Chebyshev scalar test, exact cutoff, strict nested failure intervals, and n-squared reentry quantify a practical discrete-heat stepping design problem. This is not a routine finite table: the proof covers every n>=3 and every timestep, with structural asymptotics.
